risk_reasons: Migration 120 adds four tenant tables (agent_conversations, agent_turns, agent_proposals, agent_unsupported_requests) with deny-all RLS and a hard_delete offboarding disposition.
A new BullMQ worker (AgentTurnWorker) makes a cost-guarded LLM call and owns a fenced outbox completion; a defect can double-bill or strand turns.
POST /api/operator/turns is an owner mutation route: same-origin, requireWritableOwner, account-scoped idempotency; worker step 3 re-authorizes the actor from the DB.
A new server-only feature flag OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED and an ADR 0005 flag-on envelope change (11 to 12) touch worker boot asserts.
goal: A signed-in owner can POST one Operator turn and, once the worker completes it, GET back a stored reply made of validated segments plus stored proposal and unsupported-request rows, with no review text in the model snapshot and no Apply path.
non_goals: The Operator screen, Apply, Decline, receipts, consequence line, asymmetric friction, and any UI (Run B).
applyProposal, declineProposal, patchAutoApprovalSettingsInTransaction, version-token computation at Apply, restore or undo, the policy-refused card.
A stronger or new pinned model, a pricing row, or any change to LLM_CLIENT_OPTIONS.
Tool loops, multi-turn model loops, MCP, memory tables, run-spine writes for turns.
Flipping OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED in production; the production Supabase migration is applied only at promotion, in lockstep after staging.
Tuning OutboxPoller cadence or the watchdog for turn latency.
user_visible_behavior: POST /api/operator/turns with { conversationId, clientTurnKey, locationId, text } returns { conversationId, turnId } after one transaction inserts the conversation upsert, the accepted turn, and the agent_turn outbox row via enqueueAgentTurn.
A repeat POST with the same (accountId, clientTurnKey) and same payload returns the same ids; a different payload returns 409 turn_key_conflict.
A POST without a matching Origin is rejected before any read or write; a locationId not active in the account returns 404; a conversationId owned by another account returns 404.

With OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED unset or false, POST /api/operator/turns returns 404 operator_disabled before any write, and a dispatched agent_turn job fails the turn with reason operator_disabled and completes its outbox row without loading tenant context.

AgentTurnWorker claims the turn with a 180 s lease, waits for the previous sequence in the conversation via BullMQ moveToDelayed without spending retry budget, fails the turn predecessor_stalled after 20 min, re-authorizes the actor and location from the DB, builds the snapshot for the stored location_id, makes one cost-guarded owner_operator call (validation retry once), validates, and commits reply segments + proposals + unsupported rows + outbox completion in one fenced transaction keyed on attempt_token.

GET /api/operator/turns/:id returns { status, failureReason, segments (rendered), proposals, unsupported } scoped by account; GET /api/operator/conversation?id= returns the transcript and summary reads with timestamps, and without id returns the actor's most recent conversation.
PUT /api/settings/voice accepts and GET returns highlightFacts, and the PUT writes through the shared voice writer with a businesses row lock.
A message that looks like pasted review text is stored verbatim on the turn but reaches the snapshot as [review text removed] and the reply carries the fixed server-rendered segment.

A model output that invents a count in text, claims a change was applied, references a proposal index that does not exist, proposes an operation outside the catalog or tier, or targets a scope other than the stored location or the account default fails validation.
invariants: #1 The LLM call runs only in worker/jobs/agent-turn; src/app/api/operator routes orchestrate and never import the LLM seam, the cost guard, or the worker queue registry.

#2 The turn insert and its job_outbox row commit in ONE transaction through the helper-owned topic agent_turn (enqueueAgentTurn); outbox completion is fenced on attempt_token via markOutboxCompletedIfOwned in the same transaction as the turn's terminal transition.
#15 Every module under src/lib/agents/operator and worker/jobs/agent-turn receives sql or tx explicitly; only the routes and worker/index.ts import the singleton.
The cost guard (withCostGuard) wraps every model call; the reservation precedes the call; every attempt is billed and recorded on api_costs with the owner_operator prompt version hash.
The model snapshot never carries review text, response text, or reviewer names; counts come only from reads.
The model output schema has no field for counts, approval, confirmation, or receipts.
#3 Nothing posts to Google and no auto_approval_policies row changes in this run (no executors run).
#13/#14 OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED is server-only with no NEXT_PUBLIC companion; auto-approval policy reads stay server-owned.

Every SQL statement over the four new tables carries an account_id predicate (ci:tenant-scope); the four tables are in TENANT_TABLES, TENANT_SCOPE_COLUMNS, rls-inventory, TABLE_DISPOSITIONS (hard_delete, direct_account_id, must_be_absent), purge-verification, and runContentPurgeStage.
Migration 120 is applied staging first, then production at promotion, and verified by catalogue introspection, never the Supabase migration ledger.
Structured logs carry ids only, never owner text, segments, or proposals.
edge_cases: Two dispatches of the same turn: the second claim sees status running with a live lease and exits; only the attempt whose attempt_token matches commits, so exactly one completion and one proposal set exist.
Lost first response: the browser re-POSTs with the same clientTurnKey and payload and receives the original ids, with no second turn or outbox row.

Revoked owner at step 3: the users row is gone, or its role or account_id no longer match, or the location is archived, or assertWritableSubscriptionForAccount fails: the turn is failed unauthorized or account_offboarding, no snapshot is built, no LLM call is made, the outbox row is completed.
Lease lost mid-attempt: the fenced UPDATE matches zero rows; the attempt discards its output, logs, and exits without touching the outbox row (the owning attempt completes it).

Predecessor not terminal: the claim is released (status accepted, attempt-1, attempt_token NULL) and the job is delayed with backoff via job.moveToDelayed + DelayedError; after 20 min since the predecessor's claimed_at the turn fails predecessor_stalled.
Transient failure (TransientLLMError, CostInfraUnavailableError, transient Postgres): rethrow for BullMQ retry; the claim stays and the lease expires or is released.

Terminal failure (second validation failure model_output_invalid, budget exceeded, unauthorized, operator_disabled): status failed with a user-safe reason, fenced on attempt_token, outbox completed; the BullMQ failed-hook marks the outbox failed on exhaustion only if the turn is still non-terminal.
Structured-output failure at the seam (LLMStructuredOutputError) counts as the first validation failure; the retry appends the reason to the prompt.

Pasted review detection: a star pattern (e.g. 5 stars, 5/5, five stars), a 'Reviewed by' or 'wrote:' name pattern, or a quoted block over 300 characters; the scrubbed text is used for the snapshot and the prompt; the stored owner_text is untouched.

Location named in the sentence: a scope_check segment must name a location in the snapshot list that differs from the stored location_id, and the output must carry no proposal targeting the stored location; otherwise validation fails.
Supersession: a new completed turn's proposal with the same operation and scope marks earlier pending proposals in the conversation superseded with superseded_by set.

read_pending_work star bands: one query over responses.status = 'pending_approval' (held drafts excluded via openFlagExistsSql) joined to reviews.star_rating grouped by business_id and star; NULL star counts in total only; per-location { total, byStar } plus an account total.
Star-band and posted_7d reads run after step 3 and are scoped to the stored account_id and location_id; recent completed = responses posted in the last 7 days for that location.
A conversationId the client generated that already exists under another account is a 404, never an upsert into the caller's account.
Sequence assignment takes the conversation row FOR UPDATE inside the POST transaction, so two concurrent POSTs for one conversation never share a sequence.

A JSONB read of reply, input, before, after, prepared_version_token, or receipt goes through one parser in src/lib/agents/operator/schema.ts that guards typeof string then narrows (the PgBouncer carve-out) and is listed in the lab-notes allowlist.

Set_highlight_facts is registered in the catalog with contract version 1; because no executor runs in this run, its executor is a typed stub that throws not_implemented, and the plan records that Run B replaces it.

Offboarding purge: runContentPurgeStage deletes the four tables by account_id, children first (unsupported_requests, proposals, turns, conversations), and purge verification asserts zero rows for each.

rollback_plan: Code: revert the PR; the flag OWNER_OPERATOR_ENABLED stays off in production so no route or worker path is reachable. Schema: migration 120 adds four new tables only and touches no existing table; a rollback leaves the empty tables in place (a NEW migration drops them if ever required), and the purge stage is a no-op over empty tables. Staging: reset staging to origin/main per deployment-guide.md 'Re-sync staging'.
observability: agent_turns.status and failure_reason distinguish failed reasons (operator_disabled, unauthorized, account_offboarding, predecessor_stalled, model_output_invalid, budget_exceeded).
api_costs rows with endpoint 'owner-operator' and the prompt version hash record every billed attempt.
Structured worker logs '[AgentTurnWorker]' carry turn_id, conversation_id, attempt, and outcome; the job-failure sink raises a Sentry issue on terminal exhaustion.
job_outbox rows for topic agent_turn: a stuck 'dispatched' row past the watchdog window is the signal a lease was orphaned.
